plain.en: the stone layer - the crust plus the rigid uppermost mantle

means.en: stone
layer
The rigid outer shell of the Earth, about 100 km thick. It includes the crust and the upper part of the mantle and is broken into plates.

plain.en: the weak rock just below the lithosphere

means.en: not
strong
layer
A layer about 200 km thick under the lithosphere where rock is partly molten and flows very slowly, so the rigid shell above can slide on it.

plain.en: circulating currents in hot rock

means.en: together
carrying
The movement of hotter, lighter material upward and cooler, denser material downward in a loop. In the mantle it moves rock very slowly and carries heat with it.

plain.en: the plates move toward each other

means.en: A plate boundary where two plates move toward one another. Where one is oceanic it sinks beneath the other; where both are continental neither sinks and the crust folds upward instead.

plain.en: the plates move apart

means.en: A plate boundary where two plates move away from one another. Magma rises into the gap, cools and hardens into new crust, which is how sea floor is made.

plain.en: two sides sliding past each other

means.en: A plate boundary where the two sides grind horizontally past one another. Nothing is built and nothing is destroyed, but the shaking can be strong.

plain.en: the shaking of the Earth

means.en: A Sanskrit word for earthquake. Varahamihira wrote about signs he linked with earthquakes.

plain.en: ash and rock pieces thrown out by a volcano

means.en: The rock fragments and ash thrown out of a volcano. The fine particles travel furthest and can settle hundreds of kilometres away.

plain.en: rock breaking down where it stands

means.en: Rock breaks into smaller pieces by physical, chemical or biological means. The broken pieces do not move.

plain.en: wearing away and carrying material

means.en: Soil, rock and other material worn away and carried from one place to another by agents such as water, wind, ice or waves.

plain.en: running water, waves, ice, wind and groundwater

means.en: The five things that wear land down and build it up again. Each one carries material, and each one drops it somewhere different.

plain.en: a line of equal height on a slope

means.en: A line joining points at the same height. A trench dug along one holds rainwater so that it soaks in.

plain.en: an embankment built to hold water on a slope

means.en: A low ridge of earth across a slope that stops rainwater running straight off and lets it soak into the soil instead.

plain.en: cutting flat steps into a hillside

means.en: Turning a slope into a staircase of flat treads. Each step slows the water and holds the soil.

plain.en: the Nagaland system of earthen bunds on hill slopes

means.en: An indigenous farming system that rings each field with earth banks, holding both soil and water on the slope through the monsoon.

plain.en: how steeply the bed falls

means.en: The steepness of a river bed. A steep gradient gives the water enough energy to cut a waterfall; a gentle one lets it spread out and drop its load.

plain.en: the deep pool at the foot of a fall

means.en: A deep basin dug by falling water and tumbling stones.

plain.en: the winding curve a river makes

means.en: A swing in a river's course. Water wears away the outside of each bend and drops sediment on the inside, so the swing grows wider and can be cut off.

plain.en: the stranded crescent left behind

means.en: The old loop of a meander, sealed off when the river cut straight across the neck between two bends. It is a leftover, not a new kind of river.

plain.en: the fan of new ground at a river mouth

means.en: Where a river drops its load at its mouth. If the sea cannot wash the sediment away fast enough, the land builds outward and the river splits into branches.

plain.en: the water running up the beach

means.en: The sheet of water a wave throws up the shore. It runs up further than the backwash brings back, so sand is moved landward.

plain.en: the water running back down

means.en: The thinner sheet of water draining back down the beach after the swash. It is slower and carries less, which is why sand piles up above it.

plain.en: the rocky point standing out into the sea

means.en: A tongue of high land projecting into the sea. Waves cut hardest into its exposed sides, which is where caves, arches and stacks form.

plain.en: the hollow cut into the rock

means.en: A hollow worn into the rock of a headland where waves attack a weak line. It can deepen through the headland into an arch.

plain.en: a hole through a headland

means.en: Formed when caves on opposite sides of a headland meet. When its roof falls, the outer leg stands alone as a stack.

plain.en: the pillar left when an arch falls

means.en: The outer leg of a sea arch, left standing after the roof collapses. Waves finally wear it down to a stump.

plain.en: the low block left at the end

means.en: What a sea stack becomes once the waves have worn most of it away - a low block on the wave-cut platform.

plain.en: the steep face the sea cuts into the land

means.en: A steep rock face where the sea has cut the land back. It is not the fallen rock at its foot - the debris is only what the cliff has already lost.

plain.en: the flat rock floor the cliff has retreated off

means.en: The flat bench of rock left where a sea cliff has cut back. It is the cliff's old floor, not a heap of the rubble it dropped.

plain.en: a sand bar joined to the land at one end

means.en: A long ridge of sand joined to the land at one end, with the other end in the water.

plain.en: a ridge of sand along or out from a shore

means.en: Sand laid down by waves and currents along a shore. One end can stay joined to the land while the other, the free end, lies in the water.

plain.en: the bowl-shaped hollow a glacier grinds at a mountain head

means.en: A bowl-shaped hollow with a steep headwall, cut where a glacier's head sits and grinds the floor flat while widening and deepening it.

plain.en: a sharp ridge between valleys

means.en: A sharp ridge left between hollows and valleys cut by ice.

plain.en: the broken rock and soil carried inside the ice

means.en: The load a glacier carries within itself and at its base. When the ice melts it drops the till, and what the ice carried is left behind.

plain.en: the ridge of rubble the ice drops as it melts

means.en: A ridge of rock debris left where the ice carried it and then let it go. A moraine is a record of where the ice was, not a marker of where it is now.

plain.en: the ridge at the end of a glacier

means.en: Till at the end of a glacier, marking its furthest advance. It can hold back a lake.

plain.en: the ridge along the side of the ice

means.en: A ridge of debris running along the side of a valley glacier, dumped along its edge as the ice melts back.

plain.en: the stripe down the middle where two glaciers join

means.en: A ridge running down the middle of a joined glacier, formed where the two side moraines of the tributaries meet.

plain.en: the sea flooded into a glacial valley

means.en: A flooded glacial valley. The glacier cut a flat-floored U-shaped valley, the sea later rose into it, and the water is far deeper than a river valley.

plain.en: the valley that stops in mid-air

means.en: A side valley left standing above a main glacial valley, because the main glacier cut its floor down much faster than the small glacier could.

plain.en: the valley with a wide flat floor and steep sides

means.en: A valley widened and deepened by a glacier, which grinds the floor flat and both walls at the same time, unlike a river's V.

plain.en: the ridge the wind cut out of hard rock

means.en: An elongated ridge of hard rock left standing where wind carrying sand cut the softer rock away around it.

plain.en: the polished stone

means.en: A loose stone whose surface has been cut and polished by sand carried in the wind. It is the same cutting as a yardang, at one-stone scale.

plain.en: the shallow bowl the wind scours out of the floor

means.en: A basin scoured out of desert floor by wind lifting away the finest material. Its floor can reach the water table, which is what makes an oasis.

plain.en: the flat stony floor the wind leaves

means.en: A flat lag of stones on desert floor. Once the wind has blown away everything finer, only the coarse pebbles are left behind.

plain.en: a green place where water lies close to the surface

means.en: Water and plants in a desert, where wind has lowered the ground to the water table. Many oases also get water from springs and wells.

plain.en: the long slope the sand climbs

means.en: The side of a dune facing the wind, where sand arrives and climbs. It is long and gentle.

plain.en: the short face the sand slides off

means.en: The steep lee side of a dune, past the crest. Sand cannot climb it and falls off it grain by grain.

plain.en: the crescent with horns pointing downwind

means.en: A crescent dune with its horns pointing downwind. It forms where the wind is steady and sand is scarce.

plain.en: the mound with arms in every direction

means.en: A dune with a ridge running out from it in several directions, formed where the wind direction changes.

plain.en: a U-shaped dune held by plants on its arms

means.en: A U-shaped dune. Plants hold its two arms while the bare nose moves downwind, so the arms trail behind and point upwind.

plain.en: the rock made of old shells

means.en: A rock made from the compressed remains of shells dropped on an ancient sea bed. Slightly acid water can dissolve it, which is what karst needs.

plain.en: a rock water can dissolve

means.en: Able to be dissolved in water. Only a soluble rock can be hollowed out from inside by water moving through it.

plain.en: landforms made by water dissolving rock

means.en: The name for a whole landscape, not for any single hole - caves, sinkholes and underground rivers cut into one body of soluble rock.

plain.en: the opening where the passage reaches the surface

means.en: The point at which an underground passage opens onto the surface. It is where the water carried inside the rock goes back out into the open.

plain.en: the one hanging from the roof

means.en: A mineral deposit hanging down from a cave roof, built up as dripping water leaves its load behind.

plain.en: the one rising off the floor

means.en: A mineral deposit standing up from a cave floor, built up where the same dripping water lands.

plain.en: the column where the two meet

means.en: The joined column left where a stalactite growing down and a stalagmite growing up meet.

plain.en: the empty space hollowed inside the rock

means.en: A hollow inside the rock that has not yet broken through to the surface. Water still reaches it through the joints; daylight does not.

plain.en: the bowl-shaped hole left at the surface

means.en: A bowl-shaped hollow in the ground surface where the roof of a cavity has collapsed into the space below. Doline is the second name for the same shape.

plain.en: the water crossing the cave system under the ground

means.en: A stream flowing along a passage inside the rock rather than on the surface, fed by water that soaked down through the soil above.

plain.en: the crack

means.en: A long narrow crack in the rock.

plain.en: the dye

means.en: A substance added to water in quantity too small to see, used to show where the water goes. It has no effect on the rock or the shape.

plain.en: a lake bursting out of its natural dam

means.en: Glacial lake outburst flood. A dam of ice or loose moraine gives way and the lake water is released at once.

plain.en: rock and soil sliding down a slope

means.en: A mass of rock and soil moving down a slope in one go. Rain, a cut at the foot and the loss of roots often act together.

plain.en: snow sliding suddenly down a steep slope

means.en: A mass of snow sliding off a slope. New snow loads the pack, a warm spell weakens the layer underneath, and wind piles snow unevenly.

plain.en: strong wind lifting dry soil and sand

means.en: Strong winds lifting large amounts of loose, dry soil and sand into the air.

plain.en: a natural shape on the Earth's surface

means.en: A natural feature formed by weathering, erosion, deposition or the movement of the crust, such as a mountain, valley, plain or coast.

plain.en: large moving pieces of the Earth's outer shell

means.en: Massive slabs of solid rock that make up the lithosphere and move a few centimetres a year.

plain.en: heat carried by moving material

means.en: Hot material such as magma moves upward and takes its heat with it.

plain.en: heat passing through a solid

means.en: Heat passes through rock while the rock stays where it is.

plain.en: mountains made by bent rock

means.en: Mountains formed when continental plates collide and the rock folds upward, such as the Himalaya.

plain.en: a crack where rock has moved

means.en: A break in rock along which the two sides move.

plain.en: where an earthquake starts underground

means.en: The place underground where the rock breaks. Also called the earthquake origin.

plain.en: the surface point above the focus

means.en: The point on the surface straight above the focus.

plain.en: the size of an earthquake

means.en: Each step up on the scale means about 32 times more energy.

plain.en: the belt round the Pacific

means.en: The area around the Pacific Ocean where many earthquakes and volcanoes occur.

plain.en: the dark top layer of soil

means.en: The fertile layer crops get most of their food from.

plain.en: carrying material along

means.en: A river or other agent moving what it has eroded.

plain.en: putting material down

means.en: Material settling where the water, wind or ice can no longer carry it.

plain.en: a smaller channel that splits off

means.en: A channel that leaves the main river near its mouth, as in a delta.

plain.en: a low bank beside a river

means.en: A bank built by floods when the river slows at its edge.

plain.en: flat land beside a river

means.en: Wide flat land built from sediment dropped by floods.

plain.en: a fan of river sediment

means.en: Sediment spread out, often where a steep stream reaches flat ground.

plain.en: fast rough water over rocks

means.en: A stretch of a river in its upper course.

plain.en: a ditch dug along a hill at one height

means.en: It holds rainwater so that it soaks in and recharges groundwater.

plain.en: a small dam across a stream

means.en: It slows the water and lets sediment settle behind it.

plain.en: the loose tip of a sand bar

means.en: The end of a sand bar that is not joined to the land.

plain.en: long ridges across the wind

means.en: Long dune ridges that lie across the wind, formed with one wind direction and plenty of sand.

plain.en: long ridges along the wind

means.en: Long dune ridges that lie parallel to the prevailing wind.

plain.en: the top of the wet ground

means.en: The level below which the ground is soaked with water.

plain.en: the grip between pieces

means.en: The grip that holds pieces of soil, rock or snow in place on a slope.
